facts.raw_span: A 14-year-old girl presented with a 6-year history of a photosensitive eruption involving her face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Her symptoms began at age 8 years

She had previously tried multiple medications including systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), with minimal improvement
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
Radiographic evidence of myositis
Confirmatory skin biopsy performed

Her symptoms began at age 8 years

She had previously tried multiple medications including systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), with minimal improvement
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
Radiographic evidence of myositis
Confirmatory skin biopsy performed

concepts.why: The patient's photosensitive eruption, violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, erythematous papules, and nailfold changes are consistent with dermatomyositis, and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, elevated serum IFN-β levels, and radiographic evidence of myositis support this diagnosis.

The patient's photosensitive eruption, violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, and erythematous papules could be seen in lupus erythematosus, and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies and elevated serum IFN-β levels could also be consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient's combination of dermatomyositis-like skin changes, myositis, and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies could be seen in mixed connective tissue disease.
